articles.title: ‘It was a train wreck! I was terrified’: how the new James Bond will be announced – and what can go wrong
articles.summary: As Amazon MGM Studios prepares to announce the next 007, much rides on how the news is broken. From double bookings to health and safety embarrassments, we look back at how not to do it. And then there were five.
body: A nd then there were five. While nothing has been officially announced, it is widely understood that the shortlist to replace Daniel Craig as James Bond is now down to a handful of actors: Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult.

The hunt for a new Bond comes at a propitious moment for the franchise as a whole, 25 films in (not counting the two “unofficial” entries, Casino Royale in 1967 and Never Say Never Again in 1983). After Daniel Craig stood down from the role after completing No Time to Die (in which Bond appeared to be killed in a missile strike), Amazon MGM Studios paid over $1bn to acquire “creative control” from Barbara Broccoli and Michael G Wilson, the British-American heirs to the series’ original producer Albert “Cubby” Broccoli and longtime stewards of the Bond films.

articles.title: Darth Vader’s lightsaber, used in Star Wars movies The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi, sells for nearly $5m
articles.summary: Used in the famous ‘I am your father’ scene, the on-screen prop was originally expected to sell for a fraction of the price. Auctioneers estimated it would sell for over $1m, but on Thursday a Star Wars lightsaber used by Darth Vader in the famous “I am your father” scene from The Empire Strikes…
body: Darth Vader’s saber was one of 27 lightsaber props up for sale by Heritage Auctions in the US, including ones used by Ewan McGregor’s Obi-Wan Kenobi and Hayden Christensen’s Anakin Skywalker in Revenge of the Sith.
The movie prop, which was used in the 1980 film as well as 1983’s Return of the Jedi, sold for $4.875m at an event titled “the Ultimate Star Wars auction”.

The sale marked a world auction record for any Star Wars prop used on screen, Heritage Auctions said, and surpassed the auctioneer’s previous sale of Luke Skywalker’s lightsaber and severed hand from The Empire Strikes Back, which sold for $3.75m in July.

Items up for sale spanned the far reaches of the universe created by George Lucas, including an blaster used by Boba Fett and a Yoda puppet hand used during the character’s original appearance in The Empire Strikes Back.

articles.title: How the Baltics Are Juggling a Boom in Foreign Productions Like ‘Woman Unknown’ With a Lack of Public Funds
articles.summary: Mid-October, Estonia’s long-awaited next-gen film studio complex Ida Hub, in the country’s eastern region, finally opened for business, and industry guests at Tallinn’s Black Nights Film Festival are invited to tour the facilities Nov. 21-22.
body: Ever since Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania introduced their filming incentives more than a decade ago, demand for filming in the Baltics has continued to climb, thanks to top-tier crew, competitive financial tools and varied locations. The Baltics’ enhanced visibility on global screens also coincides with momentum for Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian films and co-productions at major festivals including Sundance (“How to Divorce During the War”), Cannes (“Ulya,” “Vesna”) and Venice (“ Woman Unknown ”).
Variety has taken stock of each nation’s latest filming benefits, productions shot and challenges ahead.

The opening of the Ida Hub film complex in Ida-Viru County, in Estonia’s most northeastern region, stands as a potential game-changer for the Estonian and Baltic audiovisual business. The $18.2 million project, partly funded by E.U. coin, is a one-stop-shop where state-of-the-art filming facilities, featuring two large sound stages of 1,200 square meters (12,917 square feet) and 2,000 square meters (21,528 square feet), meet training of next-gen professionals and a tech-driven startup incubator.

articles.summary: Six more women have accused Russell Brand of sexual misconduct in a new investigation by The Times and The Sunday Times, the newspapers whose earlier reporting on the comedian features in Netflix’s just-unveiled documentary “Russell Brand: Open Secret.” The accounts were published days after Brand…
body: Brand did not respond to the new allegations. The papers said they reached out through his lawyers following his conviction, and that his lawyer reportedly mentioned the possibility of “injunctive relief” but sent no answer to the claims, even after being granted more time. Brand has denied wrongdoing in the past and has insisted that all his relationships were consensual.
According to The Times, the paper took “extensive steps” to corroborate what the women said, and none of them received payment.
The new allegations stretch from 2005 to 2015. The earliest comes from a woman, then in her mid-20s, whom Brand approached that year.
“Please I just need to have sex with you, I will pay you,” she said he told her.

articles.title: ‘Heartland’ Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir
articles.summary: Misty Jones keeps her Grammy in the fridge, alongside a near-empty Tupperware of chicken broth and, well, not a whole lot else: A former country superstar turned burnt-out rural hermit, she more or less lives off what once was, but her memories don’t exactly nourish her.
body: When a young relative goes missing, a jaded former country star returns to the industry that chewed her up in 'Country Strong' director Shana Feste's thriller, which can be gaudy fun, but eventually peters out.

It’s that hard-headed quality that her brother Donny (Paul Sparks) calls upon when he comes to her for help. His 20-something daughter Charlie (singer Carter Faith, in her film debut), herself a buzzy new talent on the Nashville country scene, has recently gone missing, and he suspects shady showbiz machinations at play — something Misty knows plenty about, even if she left that world behind long ago. And so she turns gumshoe, with an oversize felt Stetson instead of a fedora, and a lineup of men to question that range from Charlie’s too-slick-by-half manager Roy (Garrett Hedlund) to an obsessed incel stalker.

articles.title: Blink-182 to make Download debut as 2027 festival headliners
articles.summary: Evanescence and Bring Me The Horizon will also top the bill at the rock and metal festival.
body: Blink-182, Evanescence & Bring Me The Horizon have been announced as headliners of next year's Download Festival.
The trio are among more than 100 rock and metal acts set to play the event at Donington Park, Leicestershire from 9 to 13 June.
Other acts on the bill include The Prodigy, 5 Seconds of Summer and a special performance by heavy metal legends Mötley Crüe.
US pop-punk band Blink-182 will be making their Download debut, while Evanescence will become the festival's second female-fronted headliner.

articles.title: Firm offers to fake artworks for wealthy migrants seeking UK 'talent' visas - BBC investigation
articles.summary: Going undercover to expose an elaborate fraud aimed at obtaining fast-track settlement for wealthy migrants.
body: Companies are offering to help migrants pose as talented artists and tech experts to make fraudulent UK visa applications under a fast-track immigration scheme, the BBC has found.
The UK government's Global Talent visa was launched in 2020 to attract the "brightest and best" scientists and researchers from around the world. It is also open to creative artists.
Following our investigation, the Home Office is now revoking visas issued to two Nigerian men who claimed to be fine art photographers, because it believes they were obtained by deception.

Applicants for Global Talent visas are not interviewed. People granted them need to prove they are exceptionally talented or promising in their field. They can then bring their families to the UK and there is a potentially quick path to permanent residency - in three or five years.

articles.title: ‘Women and War’ Follows Four Ukrainians’ Journeys Towards Healing From Trauma (Exclusive IDFA Trailer)
articles.summary: "War does not end for these women when the weapons fall silent," highlights director Elwira Niewiera, whose doc about women going through long-term therapy premieres at IDFA in Amsterdam.
body: Four women in Ukraine who have survived Russia’s war. Four stories, including captivity, torture, sexual violence, times of hiding in dark basements, and the loss of loved ones. One shared journey – a journey toward healing. That is what the new documentary Women and War by Elwira Niewiera ( The Hamlet Syndrome, The Prince and the Dybbuk, The Domino Effect ) promises to take you on.

Women and War follows the journeys of Olena, Yuliia, Iryna, and Lena, who survived Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine. Over the course of a year, the doc shows them going through long-term therapy in the remote mountains of the country as they slowly begin to heal under the care of therapists and psychologists. And each of them must follow her own path toward recovery as they confront the lasting impact of trauma in the hope of regaiingn emotional and physical balance. Can they overcome their struggles and reclaim their lives?
